# Suspected source-file groupings (ledger)

## `ovl_11` D_80128C80 sprite initializer/draw + local helper run — 0x800CBF70–0x800CCBE8 (confidence: medium)

Candidate membership rests on the shared sprite, the allocator/dispatcher's
shared `D_80123130` direction table and corroborated call/link adjacency;
original TU boundaries remain unproven.
Evidence paths and limits: [grouping research](research/ovl_11_func_800CC4E0-grouping.md).

- ovl_11_func_800CBF70 (m) — allocates a `D_80128BB0` entry and seeds velocities from the direction table reused by `800CC7CC`.
- ovl_11_func_800CC0F8 (s) — object update/draw driver using the shared sprite.
- ovl_11_func_800CC4E0 (m) — gated object-state transition initializing the shared sprite and dispatching position-dependent effects.
- ovl_11_func_800CC6A8 (m) — stage-grid query helper resetting object state on a hit.
- ovl_11_func_800CC7CC (m) — object interaction dispatcher redirecting velocity and calling the local transition, grid-query and removal helpers.
- ovl_11_func_800CCB90 (s) — three-entry `D_80128BB0` update driver calling `800CC0F8` for occupied slots.
- ovl_11_func_800CCBE8 (m) — clears an object's item slot, then records effect coordinates or invokes item cleanup.

## `ovl_11` object archive/program pipeline — 0x800E3A3C–0x800E4428 exclusive (confidence: medium)

**Reconstructed `src/overlays/ovl_11/modules/object_archive_pipeline.c`,
all eleven entries in original order**, merging guarded_sprite_bank and
object_load_states rather than retaining protocol slices:

- E3A3C Ovl11DispatchObjectLoadPhase: sole reader of the four-handler bank,
  entered through record-slot action table element 0 at 800B94AC.
- E3A94 Ovl11GetObjectProgramCursor: exposes exactly the cursor reset by
  start/poll and stepped by run, to two opcode clients.
- E3AA4 Ovl11ReloadObjectSoundBank: consumes work +4438, which start/poll
  explicitly clear; shares current-object/far-work and graphics scratch.
- E3C04 Ovl11RequestObjectProgramRelease: selects the same phase 2 and
  clears the same dispatch scratch, through the existing reset opcode.
- E3C4C/E3CDC Ovl11ReloadGuardedSpriteBank/Ovl11UploadGuardedSpriteBank:
  complete reload/upload pair inside that pipeline interval, still published
  through its focused sprite header.
- E3D88 Ovl11GetCurrentObjectId: guarded query of the same signed id used by
  both archive-offset calculations.
- E3DC8 Ovl11StartObjectArchiveLoad, E40CC Ovl11RunObjectRecordProgram,
  E4280 Ovl11ReleaseObjectLoad, E4330 Ovl11PollObjectArchiveLoad: complete
  four-handler cycle, with private base/cursor/index and offset-table uses.

Membership is supported by that closed dispatch/state/cursor cycle and
resource-reset protocol, corroborated by contiguous original code and table
order. In the original 175C rodata blob, the sole-reader 113-opcode bank at
800B975C precedes the four-phase bank at 800B9920 without a gap. The former's
reader is E40CC, the latter's E3A3C: that reverse consumer order is consistent
with one unit emitting both tables and hence the intervening functions.
This corroboration is conditional on consumer-owned tables; an externally
compiled table-only source cannot be excluded from -G0 bytes. It is NOT a
GP ownership proof, nor does table adjacency alone prove the merge. The
sprite pair is the most independent interior service; the supported pipeline
extent carries it whole rather than manufacturing another inner boundary.
Both callback banks remain external extracted storage, not re-emitted C.

Selector order is **0 start, 1 run, 2 release, 3 poll**, not chronological
phase order: deferred start selects 3, completion 1, FF opcode 2, release 0.
Return is 0 except release's 1. The new object-archive header documents valid
indices, blocking/scratch effects, unbounded run-to-yield execution, borrowed
cursor lifetime (unchanged s32 address ABI), deferred release and the
non-boolean flag distinctions. Sound refresh restores BOTH contexts from
context zero's saved color; a cached request is left pending. The existing
sprite header stays separate for its own callers, not as a TU boundary.

EXE:80070C70 is now gObjectSoundBankRequest, with its signed halfword type
and shared-work +4438 alias retained. Its view names bankId; the descriptor
+E value remains neutral. The cursor accessor and current-id getter now use
the established Ovl11RecordCursor/Ovl11CurrentObjectId identities instead of
competing C-local extern views; no storage, pointer ABI, linkage or new alias
was introduced. Local source-global views moved to globals_override.h.
The whole-eleven checked fold first proved baseline -O2/-G0, every member
and overlay. None has an override and none was added or retired.

Lightweight, hand-maintained priors about which functions belonged to the
same original translation unit. NOT authoritative — each container's splat
config is the source of truth for actual splits; this file records *suspected*
groupings with the evidence that justifies them.

Why it matters: same-file membership has compiler-visible consequences —
shared TU-level quirks (e.g. a file-scope register variable reserving a
register for everything after its declaration point), shared idiom priors,
shared static/global data clusters, and declaration-order effects. Knowing
the group changed func_8001E9F8 from a multi-session mystery into a
15-minute solve.

Rules:
- Every group heading names its **container**. A translation unit belongs to
  one binary, and two overlays that share a RAM slot hold different functions
  at the same address — so an address range without a container names two
  different groups. The PS-X EXE is `exe`; overlay containers are `ovl_NN`,
  and their symbols carry that id as a prefix.
- Every entry cites its evidence class (shared gp-rel cluster, call graph,
  TU quirk, address adjacency, shared idiom). No evidence, no entry.
- Update in the same session that produces new grouping evidence (new
  shared global, new caller, confirmed/denied member). Correct entries that
  turn out wrong; do not let them linger.
- Confidence: high = multiple independent fingerprints; medium = one strong
  fingerprint; low = adjacency/negative evidence only.
- Match status notation: (m) matched in src/, (s) stub, (?) membership
  uncertain.

Scope: membership and evidence only. A member's role gets one line — what it
appears to do and how it relates to its neighbours. Matching technique,
debugging advice, and per-function solve detail belong in
`notes/research/` or `notes/retros/`; an active decompilation effort belongs
in its campaign note. Keep this file readable as a map.

## `ovl_11` embedded timed sprite effect — 0x80107DD0–0x80107F18 exclusive (confidence: medium)

**Module: `src/overlays/ovl_11/modules/timed_sprite_effect.c`**, reset,
start, tick and draw in original order. These four implement one four-byte
state protocol: signed animation ID at +0, signed countdown ticks at +2.
The reset writes -1/0; start writes both fields; tick decrements +2; draw
uses +0 for animation lookup and +2/10 for the reversed frame. Independently,
object lifecycle clients pass the same embedded +0xA8 or +0xE0 state to the
reset/start, tick and draw operations: D2160 updates +A8, object_render_variants
draws +A8, and C35EC/C36D0 start/draw +E0. This protocol and caller-layout
agreement, corroborated by zero-gap original order, support all four members;
no merely similar reset helper was appended. No global belongs to this unit.

`Ovl11TimedSpriteEffect` layout is in game_types.h; the API accepts raw
storage because existing callers pass several embedded record/array views.
The local duplicate Ov11Timer declaration was removed in favor of the already
shared layout before folding; the final module uses named animation/countdown
fields. Existing caller-local views need not acquire an incompatible pointer
prototype. Reset/start use external linkage as before. Tick returns 1 when
the update is suppressed by 8006C844 bit 0x08000000 as well as when already
zero, and returns 0 on the decrement that reaches zero. Drawing looks up the
full signed ID but passes only its low byte to DrawSpriteFrameRects; neither
quirk was repaired. Negative countdown inputs remain unchecked.

Reconstructed the entire six-member run as
`src/overlays/ovl_11/modules/scene_rotation_ramps.c`. The two private
record/state pairs have no users outside these six functions. Their paired
installation in 800DCA60, stepping in 800DC148, and held-phase callbacks in
800F67E0 corroborate the mirrored implementations and consecutive private
state words. This is a stronger tie than merely using the common record pool.
Renderer 800DCC5C establishes that +0x10/+0x12/+0x14 are base X/Y/Z angles:
it adds +0x20/+0x22/+0x24 and passes them to RotMatrixZXY. Thus the ramps
are Z:0..640 on flag 0x71 and Y:0..-448 on flag 0x70, in steps of 32 GTE
angle units per update call, not positions or frame counts.

Public names are `Ovl11{Init,Step}Scene{Z,Y}RotationRamp` and
`Ovl11IsScene{Z,Y}RotationRampHeld`; the header documents the four phases,
first-match selection, initialization of all three angles, missing-record
behavior, and delayed flag observation (only idle/held sample the flag).
The globals are `gOvl11Scene{Z,Y}RotationRecord` and
`gOvl11Scene{Z,Y}RotationRampState`. `gOvl11SceneRecords` names the shared
15x0x30-byte pool throughout the overlay; byte storage and all other clients'
partial views are retained. Three previously conflicting selected-record
views now use one canonical Ovl11SceneRecordRotationView in the override
header; signed angle reads are witnessed by the updates and renderer. Only
zero stores used the formerly unsigned fields. The checked baseline fold
verified all six after reconciliation, then the full campaign gate verified
all callers and every linked executable/overlay byte after renaming.

Left boundary at 800DD8AC: preceding 800DD5B0/800DD6F0 use a different private
pointer pair/state and modify pointed-to animation counters at +0x2C->+0x2E,
not these angles. Right boundary at 800DDB64: the RGB cycle has separate
private RGB/index/direction state and a scene-kind-44-only dispatch path.
These responsibility/state separations delimit the supported module, not a
proven original object boundary: -G0 provides no GP discriminator. The common
setup/update caller pair and common pool also link other independent controls;
without shared private state they do not establish a larger original TU.
All six use baseline flags; no override or policy exception was needed, no
linkage narrowed, and no storage ownership changed. Canonical identities and
published headers pass; full campaign acceptance passes with 254/2625 folded.

**Complete module reconstructed: `src/overlays/ovl_10/modules/card_diagnostics.c`,
800B889C–800BB7BC exclusive, all 22 compiled functions in original order.**
This is the PlayStation/PDA diagnostic command menu (`obj\\PdaSamp.bin`),
not a memory-card save-game UI. The driver polls pads and calls input/status;
input and status call the same dispatcher, which routes fifteen commands to
SDK Mcx wrappers, displays and hexadecimal editors. The editor pages share
one transfer buffer, command index/result text, per-page cursors and repeat
predicate. A source census finds all 64 formerly anonymous writable/table
identities used here only in this module. The call closure, private context,
resident pointer tables and interleaved member-order literal/table pool
support the whole unit; no smaller slice was accepted. -G0 supplies no GP
ownership proof. Both outer text boundaries are structural: the first game
instruction in the container and the final function's end at the data window.

The complete original rodata pool is now reproduced from C at file 4..A79:
inline help/status strings retain one shared newline/color identity through
cc1's TU-wide constant cache; the transfer-mode/day labels referenced only by
resident pointer tables are named const objects at their original emission
positions. They are real string data, not padding arrays. The 30-byte default
result message keeps its packed-copy view. All zero alignment comes from the
compiler; no source padding, new data allocation, asm or flag was introduced.
The unreferenced leading word (0..4) and non-NUL three-byte tail (A79..A7C)
remain extracted, with no invented ownership. Resident writable pointer
arrays remain in the original data blob and still point at exactly the same
string bytes. A unique relocated whole-section proof established 4..A79,
including every compiler-generated switch-table word and every literal.

The checked fold compiles all 22 at baseline -O2/-G0, oracle-checks each
member and verifies the entire ovl_10 image byte-for-byte. Its first write
exposed a concrete helper assumption: it required the proved pool to start
at the old first-table attribution and did not anticipate the generator's
subalign 1 for an odd tail. `foldTranslationUnit.ts` now admits only a uniquely
proved full pool, rejects crossed nonmember attributions, retains its unowned
edge residues and derives input alignment by the same split-position rule as
bootstrapOverlay. The exact pool and all 22 then passed the checked fold.
This is a scoped shared-tool fix outside the source integration roots, not
a bypass of byte proof or a TU boundary at a table.

All functions now have scoped Ovl10 behavior names. The public header
`ovl10_card_diagnostics.h` publishes only Ovl10RunPdaCommandMenu and documents
its blocking frame loop, Mcx/pad prerequisites, Select exit, state lifetime,
shared-buffer and unchecked-length constraints. L2/L1 select, Start submits.
The input reads PadInputState.pressedButtons (+8), not heldButtons: per-bit
counters advance only while their supplied bit is present, so their tick
predicate must not be documented as elapsed hold time. The existing packed
text-copy widths, declaration visibility, external linkage and field types
are retained. SDK declarations come from their canonical headers.

Command selection is canonically signed (the %15 arithmetic); dispatch keeps
its explicit unsigned interpretation. The common result is a 64-byte char
buffer with per-copy packed views, not three incompatible global types. The
other 64 data identities have scoped command/editor/buffer/table names at
their original addresses. C-local externs moved to globals_override.h, the
time weekday table has its witnessed char-pointer view, and obsolete
rodata externs are removed. Naming does not equate another overlay's identical
RAM addresses, create ownership definitions for writable data or infer static
linkage. The public interface audit reports zero failing sites.

## Sprite / tile-load wrappers — 0x80017042–0x8001782C (confidence: medium)

Sprite data decompressor and thin callers, address-adjacent to the tile
loader func_8001782C. func_80017300 is a raw-compression sprite decompressor
(poly-flag-driven byte/RLE copy into D_8005EE28 followed by LoadImage +
DrawSync); it is reached by the four thin wrappers func_8001719C,
func_800171CC, func_80017200, func_80017240, and neighbouring func_80017284
links it to the sprite family by calling func_80015AAC / func_80015B24 plus
the tile loader func_8001782C (which func_80016B7C also calls). Evidence:
address adjacency inside one gap, shared LoadImage/sprite-idrom idiom, and
the func_80017284 bridge to the sprite/animation family. TU boundary
uncertain; func_80017300 uses split addressing (lui+%lo hi kept in a saved
register), so it does not carry the renderer TUs' -mno-split-addresses flag.

D_8005E3C0 (the *active* context pointer) is read by 36 functions across the
binary; that is "this function draws", not a grouping signal.

Practical consequence for anyone matching a member: a gp-relative access in
the target is a membership signal, and a member must *declare* the symbols it
reaches that way. Non-members must not. See
`plans/toolchain-native-small-data-addressing.md` for how that is expressed in
source.

## func_8001A284 — member of the 0x8001A574 family TU (MATCHED 2026-08-15)

Dispatch-style switch on `arg0 & 0xFFF` (cases 10-34) returning a pointer or
value. TU evidence: calls func_8001A574 and func_8001A870 (same family's
callees), reaches the 0xB8-stride D_800749F8 array (family fingerprint) and
D_8005F0F8 (sentinel, split address form), and touches the
`&D_8006C838 + 0x8000` region at offsets 0x676C/0x19CA/0x19CE/0x6620/0x26DA
and `&D_8006C838 + 0x81F0` / `+ 0x7AB8` (0xB8/0xB4-stride scans). Owns
D_8005E490 GP-relatively (tentative definition in this file). Matched
byte-identically; the earlier parked analysis of case 15's exit structure
(goto into case 10, D_80071A00 <= -G8 override) was WRONG and its override
has been removed. What the bytes actually are:

- Case 15's inner dispatch is a NESTED SWITCH on the 0x676C halfword
  (cases 0/1/2, default result=0), not an if-chain. The balanced
  compare order in the target (==1 first, then <2, ==0, ==2) is GCC's
  small-switch dispatch fingerprint.
- Case 10 and the nested case 0 both return `&D_8006C838 + 0x51C8`
  (there is no D_80071A00 reference at all). Case 10 spells it inline;
  jump2's cross-jump equivalence rewrite (find_cross_jump's REG_EQUAL
  path) folds both copies to the same la-const, merges the arm into
  case 10's copy, and leaves case 10's expander HIGH orphaned — that is
  the "stray lui v0,0x8007" at 0x8001A2C0. See
  notes/research/func_8001A284-crossjump-equiv-orphan.md.
- Cases 22/23 share a named `neg1 = -1` sentinel local; case 22 sets it
  before the load (so it conflicts with the base in v0 and allocates
  v1), case 23 after (so it fills the load-delay slot).
- Case 33 carries a zero-instruction scheduling barrier (tracked debt,
  allowlisted): the target births the `addiu a1,gp,%gp_rel(D_8005E490)`
  argument before the base formation and every clean hoist spelling is
  CSE-folded back to the call site.
- The TU's .rodata is the 25-entry jump table plus a 4-byte zero pad at
  0x940; splat.yaml carries a `[0x940, rodata]` sub-split for the pad.
  Both lines (and the whole game-rodata block) are now derived by
  `tools/build/deriveRodataSplits.ts` (attribution iff the owner is
  compiled C; extent = the owner's .o .rodata size, which produces pad
  residues mechanically). The original hand edit by the autoloop —
  attributing 0x8DC while the function was still a stub — is exactly the
  inconsistent state the tool's check mode rejects.

**Five-entry sprite-submission service reconstructed as
`modules/scene_sprite_draw.c`, 800BAE20–800BB0F8 exclusive.** E20/EA0/EEC
share comparison-before-animation-selection and call BAFFC with their source
and halfword position; F70 is the fixed centered-rect variant. BAFFC alone
uses the private BCD18/BCD20 projection scratch and applies the additional
screen pass only to scene-record sources 0/1/2/5. The dispatch surface is
A510/A5D0/A670 plus A4F0; A510 also calls BAFFC directly. The common private
leaf/workspaces, variant protocol and gapless order support the complete
five-entry set, not the broad C0448 work area by itself.

Left entity_record_views serves entity IDs, per-entity fields and sprite-ID
lookup, not this source/position/submission protocol. Right scene_resources
initializes camera, geometry and retained sprite banks; its initialization
of the primary source is a loader/client link, not private projection-state
ownership. Neither neighboring service shares BCD18/BCD20 or the leaf
protocol. No stronger extension witness was found. Both are conservative
-G0 service cuts, not GP proofs; no override creates an internal boundary.

Names: Ovl21DrawRecordSprite/DrawSlotSprite/DrawPrimarySceneSprite,
DrawCenteredFrameRects and SubmitProjectedSprite. The public
`ovl21_scene_sprite_draw.h` records raw record/slot ABIs, signed-selector
versus low-byte setter behavior, halfword world offsets, unchecked six-entry
X/Z table, OT placement, draw-then-update ordering and non-reentrant scratch.
Globals are gOvl21SpriteProjectPosition/Screen, FrameRectSprite and
SceneOffsetPairs, preserving sizes/views. BCD20 remains a separate raw symbol
for ovl_25's unrelated load-stage byte at the same RAM address; no overlay
identities were conflated. The unprototyped internal leaf declarations are
replaced by its real shared signature; external linkage is unchanged. All
five and the linked overlay passed the baseline fold, without compiler flags
or new policy exceptions.

**Reconstructed `modules/scene_draw.c`, 800BA4C0–800BA698 exclusive:**
all five entries, Ovl21DrawSceneSprites, DrawSceneFrame, DrawRecordSprites,
DrawActiveSlotSprites and DrawPrimarySpriteAtSelectedOffset. The composite
calls the three walkers in fixed order; those walkers have no other call
clients. The separate frame wrapper is paired with the composite by the
interaction controller, implementing the same scene drawing pass. These
exclusive traversal calls and shared record/slot protocol support the group,
not simple adjacency or the large scene state alone. Left A300 advances
projectile positions/lifetimes and clears expired slots; it neither calls this
traversal nor is called by it. The scene controller coordinates update and
drawing. Right A698 scans the same slots for a nearby active entry, but has
no drawing/helper role. These neighbors corroborate the shared scene format,
not exclusive membership in the drawing closure. These are
conservative -G0 reconstruction cuts, not original-file proofs, and do not
rest on A698's outstanding compiler flag. The wider scene file is uncertain.

ovl21_scene_draw.h publishes the two scene-level entries and documents six
records, three slots, marker triggering/offset, draw order, source mutation
and render-state prerequisites. Internal walkers retain external linkage;
locals name record/slot cursors without changing types or arithmetic. The
signed-halfword primary offset selector is gOvl21PrimarySpriteOffsetIndex;
its extern moves from C into globals_override.h with load-width evidence.
The earlier gOvl21RecordObjectBase rename required explicit reconciliation
of its shared-header extern after canonicalization; the initial checked fold
reported that undeclared anchor and rolled back. With that declaration fixed,
the whole five-entry fold and overlay pass at baseline -O2/-G0. No flags,
new exceptions, storage or scope collisions were introduced.

non-growth. Exit 1 reflects the incomplete campaign, not a verification failure.

controllers and all 81 write/read/slot-transfer stages. A whole-source census
corrects the older EA18 interface-cut rationale: MenuState, MenuExitRequest,
MonitoredCard, SelectedCard, SelectedSlot, CardStates and MenuStateTimer
(all gOvl15-prefixed) occur in exactly these two former modules, not in the
UI/card/save services. Reset initializes their shared context; controllers
reset/advance the saturating timer when stages change state; stages consume
that timer, change state and request exits. Stages also call the same reset,
so this is a cyclic private protocol, not merely three public service calls.
The three dispatchers and every stage have no other source clients. These
positive state/call witnesses supersede the older conservative EA18 cut.

Left is the overlay's first text entry, after its rodata. Right 32A8C starts
the row-placement/record-pool service: it uses none of those seven controls,
owns separate placement tables and staged records, and serves the menu by
allocation/stage/restore operations rather than menu-stage callbacks. Its
other staged-record client is nonadjacent 13468C. No extension across that
service is established; the later 1335F8 flag is not this boundary's reason.
Overlays use -G0, so these are private-protocol/link-order witnesses, not
claimed GP-proven historical object edges. No private linkage was inferred.

The checked full-85 baseline fold passed every member and linked ovl_15,
including the unchanged mixed switch-table/SC-literal pool at file 4..22C.
The controllers add no rodata; no flag, ownership or type change was needed.
`ovl15_save_menu.h` now publishes only reset and the three scene controllers;
the three no-outside-client dispatcher headers are retired and their timing,
card-monitoring, drawing and exit contracts are local to the module.
8012E7C8 is now Ovl15UpdateCardTransferScene: its actual dispatcher selects,
validates and transfers slot records, optionally writes the result, and does
not restore the persistent image like plain read. Its old WithSprites name
only described a resource-loading side effect. The original overlay identity,
ABI, external linkage, widths and all state behavior remain unchanged.

Final acceptance: `tuProgress.ts --verify --no-cache --baseline
build/tu-campaign/baseline.json` passes all eight integrity gates, including
the EXE/all thirteen overlays, data, callback and jump-table bytes, canonical
interfaces, source policy and exception non-growth. Folded membership stays
2345/2625; merging the two supported slices reduces valid module TUs from
473 to 472. No new flags, permissions, stubs or tooling changes were needed.

Earlier integration history follows; its EA18 boundary is superseded above.

**Completed wider `modules/card_menu_states.c`, 8012EA18–80132A8C exclusive:
all 81 write/read/slot-transfer entries, in original order.** The 25 write
stages absorb the entire previous 56-entry card_read_states module. These
are three complete dispatcher/stage closures, not just the repeated text
prologue: each dispatcher has one scene-controller caller, each internal
stage belongs to its dispatcher's table, and the workflows share card-cache,
selection, prompt and timer protocols. The interleaved SC literal and all
switch tables emit one exactly reproduced pool at file 4..22C. Overlays are
-G0; this is closure/private-protocol/pool evidence, not a GP ownership proof.

The old 301A0 cut was solely a literal-representation limit. Writing the
consumer-owned three-byte "SC" signature as a literal gives the full merged
source its original emission; the following type store overwrites its NUL.
No artificial padding data was added. Unique relocated whole-pool proof
allows the checked fold to absorb the D4 signature/alignment gap and both
old zero alignment gaps; all 81 functions and ovl_15 bytes pass at baseline.
No override or policy exception was added or removed.

Left EA18 is an evidence-limited interface cut against save_menu_lifecycle:
the three outward scene controllers own last-stage tracking and lifecycle
state (gOvl15LastMenuState and 80137590), resource/fade/draw/exit pacing and
call only the three stage dispatchers. The 81 own the format-prompt substate,
icon-offset consumer and SC literal; none joins lifecycle's exclusive state
or emitted data. The shared remaining menu words also serve UI/card/save
services and alone do not extend the unit. No original compiler boundary is
proved here, but there is no private-helper/state/pool witness to extend it.
Right 32A8C starts the separately published row-placement/record-pool service;
all dispatcher targets/stages end before it, and transfers call its allocation,
staging and restore operations through that service, not as additional stages.
The later 335F8 no-GCSE issue is NOT the reason for this boundary. A stronger
future link-order/private-data witness may still justify a larger unit.

Write functions now have scoped Ovl15CardWrite names paralleling read and
transfer, with numeric PromptStateNN names only where prompt meaning is
undecoded. The shared format-confirmation step and three-by-three icon frame
offsets are named without changing widths or storage. Seven missing text
externs moved to globals_override.h with consumer evidence; duplicate C
externs were removed. All text calls use EXE:8001AC10's matched u32* contract,
not incompatible per-function void*/u32* declarations. Only the new write
frame entry is published in ovl15_card_write_states.h; existing read/transfer
headers remain the other two interfaces. interfaceAudit reconciled the one
lifecycle caller and proved its object unchanged. Internal stages retain
external linkage; folding was not used to invent static linkage.

**Batch verification:** tuProgress --verify --baseline
build/tu-campaign/baseline.json passes all eight integrity gates, the EXE and
all 13 overlays including data, callbacks, tables and placement. All 363
modules are valid; folded count rises 2130 → 2156 (469 remain). The same
batch completes ovl_31's six-entry module. Canonical names, published
interfaces, source policy and exception non-growth pass. No commit made.

The following is the earlier partial-fold history, superseded by this union.

**Expanded/merged as `modules/card_read_states.c`, 801301A0–80132A8C
exclusive, all 56 entries in original order.** It absorbs the initially
verified 35-entry card_read_sprite_states module plus the complete preceding
21-entry plain-read dispatcher/stage set; neither closed scene is sliced.
The two machines share the private monitor/context and duplicate prompt
protocol, now represented together. The new public Ovl15StepCardReadMenu
header documents restore/exit behavior separately from the transfer entry.
The helper's section-relative alignment correction (see the whole-ovl_19
section) proves and pools the zero at file 158, eliminating the former cut
at 31094. Their pooled table block is F4–22C, in original member order.
All 56 and the complete overlay passed the checked baseline fold. The
second full campaign gate also passes every integrity check at 1359 folded
functions and 205/205 valid modules, including the executable's named ovl_19
callback and all data/placement. No compiler flag or source-policy exception
was added or retired.

The entire 81-entry write/read/transfer union remains a plausible wider TU.
Its unresolved nonzero SC signature/padding at file D4 is a mechanical
literal-emission limit, not evidence for an original boundary at 301A0. A
fresh dry run of all 81 after the final gate confirms the sole current first
refusal: `the members' jump tables are not contiguous: - [0xD4, rodata] lies
between them`. Next useful experiment: recover that consumer-owned signature's
C emission/layout, then retry the whole union; do not invent an original cut.
The earlier zero at 68 is the same section-relative alignment class, no longer
an asserted obstacle. Right 32A8C starts row-placement and has no stage/monitor
protocol. Thus the current left boundary explicitly records the remaining
representation limit rather than inventing a per-scene original file.

Initial 35-entry integration details (still applicable to the transfer half): The dispatcher and its complete
34-stage closure form the card-read/slot-transfer scene, not just the handlers
sharing the historical text prologue. No outside function calls an individual
stage. Three jump tables at file 174/1FC/214 pool in member order through 22C.
The shared lifecycle calls only Ovl15StepCardTransferMenu; its header explains
frame stepping, card monitoring, asynchronous I/O, checksum/slot-transfer
stages and shared menu state. All entries have scoped CardTransfer names;
undecoded prompts retain their stage numbers instead of invented text meaning.
The alternating channel is gOvl15MonitoredCard, still a signed halfword used
by all three dispatchers. Capacity arrays now name each side's selected
categories, populations and limits without changing their signed widths.

Boundary qualification: the preceding read-only scene has its own complete
20-stage closure and restarted state numbering; none of those stages calls
this scene's stages. Right 32A8C begins the separate row-placement helper.
Neither is an omitted stage of this dispatcher. Nevertheless the three scene
machines share narrow monitor/menu storage and duplicated prompt templates,
so one original file for their full 81-entry union remains plausible. The
initial left boundary was NOT an original TU proof. Its former raw-zero
limits at 68/158 are resolved by the section-relative alignment guard; only
D4's eight-byte SC signature/padding still blocks the full three-scene union. The folded scene is the entire closed
stage unit presently representable; those emission/ownership questions must
be solved before accepting the wider merge, not protected as historical cuts.
The record-pool editor/serializer is called as an external service and has its
own still-unresolved 335F8 compiler-setting/context question.

The first checked fold rolled back on incompatible void*/u32* declarations
of EXE:8001AC10. Reusing its matched u32* contract allowed the baseline fold
to preserve every member and all ovl_15 bytes. Seventeen text-bank externs
moved from C to globals_override.h with individual address/caller evidence;
the existing Ovl15CardFilename storage binding replaces its local raw alias.
The inherited 35C20 declaration conflict was investigated, not hidden: every
callee exit returns a constant in 0..12, so its signed-halfword status return
is supported and preserves its existing constant returns. Its word parameter
and explicit input narrowing remain intact. interfaceAudit then reconciled
all six affected caller units, adding the existing halfword argument conversion
where needed and proving unchanged objects. No flag was applied or retired.
Final batch `tuProgress --verify --baseline build/tu-campaign/baseline.json`
passes every integrity gate: 1296 folded functions, 211/211 valid modules,
all EXE and 13 overlay bytes including data/placement, canonical names and
affected interfaces, policy, convergence and exception non-growth. The status
service's changed return declaration and every affected caller are included.
No extra compiler permission, assembly, register binding or stub was added.

## `ovl_25` leaf run — 0x800BB970–0x800BBA7C (two supported services, not one established TU)

The former four-entry hypothesis separates into two coherent modules. The
only proposed join between BB9D0 and BBA30 was a sign-extension/absolute-base
leaf prologue: that is an ABI idiom, not evidence of common compilation.
There is no private data or call edge across that seam.

- **`src/overlays/ovl_25/modules/record_value_increments.c`**, BB970/BB9D0:
  same indexed 0x1D4-stride records, adjacent +19EA/+19EC values, and the
  same B9208 caller applies both services in one block. Names
  `Ovl25RaiseRecordByteRangeValue`/`Ovl25RaiseRecordHalfwordRangeValue`;
  `ovl25_record_value_increments.h` records unchecked signed indices,
  signed-versus-unsigned comparisons, steps 20/500 and caps 255/65535.
  Head at BB970 follows the animation-slot lifecycle, which accesses
  different arrays and has no edge to this pair. Tail at BBA30 changes to
  render-context RGB, with no work-record access. These are conservative
  boundaries from independent protocols, not GP-proven boundaries (-G0).
- **`src/overlays/ovl_25/modules/background_color_pingpong.c`**, BBA30/BBA7C:
  setter plus its direct interpolation-driver caller, backed by the private
  direction/index and endpoint triples. Names `Ovl25SetBackgroundColor` and
  `Ovl25StepBackgroundColorCycle`; both published in
  `ovl25_background_color_cycle.h`. The head is the protocol seam above;
  the tail is the overlay text/data boundary at BBB40 (0x800BBB40).
  Original data at BCD50/BCD52 is the signed direction/index pair, and
  BCDAC/BCDB8 holds RGB (0,99,127)/(0,165,213), confirmed in the original
  overlay at offsets 4F8C/4F98. Canonical names are
  `gOvl25BackgroundCycleDescending`, `gOvl25BackgroundCycleIndex`,
  `gOvl25BackgroundCycleLowRgb`, `gOvl25BackgroundCycleHighRgb`.
  Declarations now live in globals_override.h (triples as s32[3], not
  scalar-first-word views), with all uses propagated. Rendering still
  narrows components to bytes and enables clearing in both contexts;
  update-before-step and endpoint repetition are documented.

Both complete folds passed at baseline; neither adds a flag, changes
linkage or defines shared work/render storage. The historical evidence
below is retained to distinguish the two real relationships from the
rejected prologue-only join.

Candidate same-TU run of `ovl_25` at file offsets 0x3B50–0x3D20. Evidence is a
gapless link run whose call graph agrees with it, a shared leaf-prologue idiom,
and a shared-global cluster at the head of the run.

Fingerprints:
- address adjacency: `ovl_25_func_800BB970` (0x60, ends 0x3BB0) sits immediately
  before `ovl_25_func_800BB9D0` (0x60, ends 0x3C10), which sits immediately
  before `ovl_25_func_800BBA30` (0x4C, ends 0x3C5C), which is followed directly
  by `ovl_25_func_800BBA7C` (0xC4, ends 0x3D20, then the overlay data segment) —
  contiguous, no unrelated code between;
- shared-global cluster: `ovl_25_func_800BB970` and `ovl_25_func_800BB9D0` both
  address `D_8006C838`, both scale the sign-extended s16 argument by exactly
  0x1D4 with the identical `sll/subu/sll/addu/sll/addu/sll` chain, both add an
  identical `ori $zero,0x8000` base offset, and both touch adjacent halfwords
  of the same 0x1D4-stride record (`+0x8000+0x19EA` vs `+0x8000+0x19EC`);
- call graph agrees with link order: `ovl_25_func_800BBA7C` issues
  `jal ovl_25_func_800BBA30` (at 0x3C9C), and the callee immediately precedes
  the caller;
- shared leaf-prologue idiom: `ovl_25_func_800BB9D0` and `ovl_25_func_800BBA30`
  both open with `sll $a0,16` / `sra $a0,16` (a sign-extended s16 first

Non-evidence for the tail: `ovl_25_func_800BBA30` writes `D_8005E5E8` (a cross-container

of `ovl_25_func_800BBA30` matches matched `ovl_11_func_800DC114` 13 of 13

## `ovl_25` 8×0x16 record-array initializer/consumers/handlers — 0x800BB4B4 / 0x800BB580 / 0x800BB628 / 0x800BB788 / 0x800BB874 (confidence: medium)

**Module: `src/overlays/ovl_25/modules/vram_animation_slots.c`**, all six
entries BB4B4/BB510/BB580/BB628/BB788/BB874, through BB970 exclusive.
BB510 requests descriptors through BB874; BB580 dispatches the same slot
array to BB628/BB788. Initializer, acquisition, descriptor field remapping,
update-mode dispatch and shared storage establish the complete slot lifecycle,
corroborated by link order. This is not a grouping based only on a global.

Names follow the already-established ovl_11 protocol but remain distinct

**Paired projection service reconstructed as
`src/overlays/ovl_19/modules/projected_sprite_render.c`,
ovl_19:800BADF8–800BB08C exclusive**, both original entries:
Ovl19DrawProjectedSprite (BADF8) and Ovl19DrawProjectedSpriteState (BAFAC).
Both adjust the input position to the surface, fill a private three-halfword
projection vector, project into a two-word screen buffer, depth-bucket a
sprite submission and submit the same companion sprite. The first retains
caller Y adjustment and source-identity special cases; the second selects
an animation first. Their paired output buffers at BD048/BD050 and input
vectors at BD080/BD088 are consecutive, same-sized scratch objects used only
by these members. BA770/BA834/BAB4C form their actual client family. This
paired data/projection/submission protocol, not shape similarity or adjacency
alone, supports the join at BAFAC. The four scratch globals now carry semantic
container-owned names without moving or defining any storage.

Boundary at BADF8: preceding BADAC is a stateless value-label offset lookup,
using only the private BCFF8 table and no projection/surface/draw helper. Its
clients are the value-table display and B8C74, not this pair. BAD50 draws a
fixed UI sprite and has no shared projection scratch. Their data adjacency
alone does not include them. Boundary at BB08C: the following nested helper
and Ovl19DrawValueTable have their own proven static-chain relationship,
label text/offset protocol and field_D8 slots, with no use of this scratch.
The left render-driver clients are separated by the independent actor-control
service and two leaves; no evidence supports absorbing those intervening
functions just to co-locate callers. These are conservative protocol/data cuts,
not GP-proven original TU boundaries (-G0); a wider original object remains
unproven, not declared impossible.

The public ovl19_projected_sprite.h keeps both ABIs and documents mutable
surface-adjusted input coordinates, pixel offsets, OT slot arithmetic,
source-specific companion behavior, unchecked projection/OT bounds and shared
scratch non-reentrancy. Parameters/locals name the demonstrated submission
roles without assigning a gameplay meaning to the companion sprite. Five
caller/declaration carriers now include the header; no linkage was narrowed,
no data ownership changed, and no old live function alias remains.

The complete pair first passed the checked baseline -O2/-G0 fold. No flag
or policy exception exists for either member. Projection/trails batch
acceptance: `tuProgress.ts --verify --baseline build/tu-campaign/baseline.json`
passes all integrity gates, 936 folded / 147 valid modules, including every
linked EXE/overlay/data byte, interfaces, source policy and exception non-growth.

Historical [paired render helper/caller evidence](research/ovl_19_func_800BAFAC-grouping.md).

**Reconstructed the complete 22-entry 800DE9C8–800DFC44 run as
`modules/code160_record_handlers.c`, not a predicate-only slice.** Original
address suffixes, in order: DE9C8/DEB00/DEEE0/DEF30/DF010/DF0F8/DF128/
DF228/DF3BC/DF400/DF4F0/DF51C/DF5AC/DF614/DF6A8/DF72C/DF84C/DF9F0/

is real action-bank slot 14 and remains in the module.

Membership: the active predicate DF4F0 has thirteen callers, all inside this
interval: DE9C8, DEB00, DEEE0, DEF30, DF128, DF51C, DF5AC, DF614, DF6A8,
DF72C, DF84C, DF9F0 and DFB98. E0AFC no longer calls it; the old wider-caller

11/12/13/14 from this run, with no other clients of those callbacks. DEF30,
DF400, DF228 and DEEE0 form the tick/source/selection helper closure. DE9C8
and DEB00 are the pool lifecycle's paired update passes over the same B8
record, predicate, opacity/effect and timer/flag protocol. DF0F8 is the
unconditional B8 clear twin of the initializer (external clients, no private
call edge); DF3BC is the sole accessor for its adjacent descriptor data and
is used by presentation outside the run. Those two members' exact historical
co-compilation is weaker than the helper/callback core, but no internal edge
is supported at either and they lie inside the core's closed caller span.
Data/table order corroborates the closure; it is not GP proof under -G0.

Left code160_record_creation allocates records and calls this initializer but
uses none of the private predicate/timer/handler machinery. Right
animation_sequences begins at DFC44 with a distinct callback bank and playlist
protocol; the dispatcher intentionally consumes that separate public bank.
The final DFC3C belongs to this action bank, not to animation_sequences.
No exclusive helper/state witness extends either edge. These are
protocol/table-supported reconstruction boundaries, not recovered original
object edges, and no flag or mechanical limit supplied either cut.

Names preserve every original overlay/address identity. Ovl11UpdateCode160RecordLiveness, StepCode160RecordFrame, TickCode160Record,
DispatchCode160Handler,
Clear/InitCode160Record, SelectCode160RecordSpriteSource and
ReadCode160SpriteDescriptor describe the published lifecycle/source interface.
The private predicate, selector, state-code helper and eleven handlers have
behavior/bank-slot names. The two 20-entry pointer banks are

`gOvl11Code160SpriteDescriptors` is 0x90 bytes, **nine** rows of four u16 pairs,
not eighteen rows of pairs. Its animation/frame type reuses the corroborated
Ovl11StateSpriteFrame view. Data/callbacks remain extracted at original
locations; no new C storage or static linkage was inferred.

The first baseline checked fold rolled back on concrete conflicting dispatcher
prototypes and a duplicate prefix typedef. Reusing game_types.h's exact prefix,
adding the demonstrated Ovl11Code160HandlerRecord view and publishing one
pointer contract resolved this, with explicit compatible pointer casts and
unchanged caller objects measured by interfaceAudit (22 unit changes over eight
published callees). The private alternate predicate declaration now uses that
same prefix. Raw bank/blob externs were reconciled to the existing override
views rather than redeclared in C. The descriptor extern likewise moved to the
override header. The source retains the initializer's packed unaligned pair
copy, counter widths, loaded-bank addressing and original function order.

A further affected-interface correction replaces DFB98's old five-scalar
800D05D0 declaration/call with its matched definition's pointer plus padded
four-word vector BY VALUE. The vector's unused fourth word remains untouched.
This canonical aggregate contract, named position/record locals and documented
movement behavior preserve exact bytes; no incompatible-prototype workaround
was added. The remaining unrelated existing interface disputes are unchanged.
The module header documents update-count units, source/table prerequisites,
20-entry unchecked handler indices, repeat suppression, animation selection

## `ovl_11` D_80123DFC two-entry callback-table cluster — 0x80123DFC (confidence: low)

**Reconstructed `modules/map_grid_cells.c`, six entries DA638–DAFD4
exclusive.** Neighborhood classification at DA638 and refresh at DACD4
share the exact kind-36/state-byte/low-nibble texture protocol and call the
local checked accessor DAF60; their span carries effect placement DAC08,
random matching DADB0 and kind-pair normalization DAF24 in original order.
The latter two also use that map-entry protocol, not a different private
system. Private 3x3 offset/bounds tables and coordinate/variant scratch
belong to DA638. The two-entry texture-setter table is shared with other
map services, so it is corroboration, not private-state ownership proof.
The inverted selector of random search is documented, not silently unified.

Left DA588 installs sprite-source records from 80125528/800957F8 for the
asset loader, with no cell accessor/texture/helper state; right DAFD4 begins
coordinate_clamp's private bounds/reset/clamp protocol. Neither supplies a
positive private-state or helper extension. These are evidence-limited
protocol cuts under -G0; no historical TU boundary is claimed from adjacency
alone. The nearby reset/random entry transitions and distant grid walkers
are clients of shared services, not proof that all intervening code is one TU.

The six function names and header ovl11_map_grid_cells.h describe checked
access, neighborhood variants, state refresh, randomized matching, kind-pair
normalization and effect placement. Inputs, inverse selector, wildcard bits,
last-hit outputs, 400-unit spacing and shared scratch are documented. Globals
name the setter table, bounds, nine offset pairs and probe coordinates/variant.
The coordinate data word is now two named halfword labels; its existing
second-halfword assembler identity remains first+2, preserving address birth.
The alternate-grid search view moved to globals_override.h without changing
its base origin, gate width or layout. Original nested classification tests,
including odd fallback comparisons, remain unchanged. The existing DAC08
memory-clobber exception is carried, not added or broadened. All six and
the linked overlay passed the checked baseline -O2/-G0 fold; no flag changed.
Interface publication exposed DAC08's s32 definition versus 876C's void
contract; all observed clients discard its result. Publishing void and
calling the pool without returning its value reconciles every caller while
retaining every callee/caller byte, as the full gate proves. This is a
verified interface correction, not a cast bypass or incompatible declaration.
